data.title: MS&AD Insurance Earnings Decline In H1
data.description:
TOKYO (dpa-AFX) - MS&AD Insurance Group Holdings, Inc. (MSADY, 8725.T), an insurance holding company, on Thursday reported a decline in net income in the first half of 2026 compared with the previous year. The company raises its full year outlook.

For the first half, net income attributable to owners of the parent declined 17.3 percent to 363.73 billion yen from 439.58 billion yen in the previous year.

Earnings per share were 252.62 yen versus 292.26 yen last year.

Insurance revenue increased to 3.41 trillion yen from 3.09 trillion yen in the previous year.

Looking ahead, the company expects net income attributable to owners of the parent to be 490 billion yen, up from previous guidance of 425 billion yen.

For the full year, basic earnings per share is anticipated to be 343.56 yen, up from previous guidance of 295.75 yen.

MS&AD Insurance Group closed trading 1.94% lesser at JPY 5,061 on the Tokyo Stock Exchange.

data.title: Singapore Stocks' Upward Catalysts Appear Largely Priced In — Market Talk
data.description: Singapore equities' upward catalysts appear to be largely priced in, say Citi analysts in a note. Singapore's banking sector, which makes up more than half of the benchmark FTSE Straits Times Index's weight, is likely to struggle to drive the stock market higher, they say, as dividend yield spreads are likely compressing to decade lows amid tightening net interest margins, higher funding costs and softer wealth momentum. The analysts recommend rotating positions away from crowded cyclical stocks toward value and defensive names, such as CapitaLand Integrated Commercial Trust and SATS. Citi rates Singapore equities underweight relative to it Southeast Asian peers into 1H and has a FTSE STI target of 5325. The index is 0.4% higher at 5077.19. (megan.cheah@wsj.com)

data.title: Fed Likely to Deliver Two More Rate Hikes in Near Future — Market Talk
data.description: Goldman Sachs reiterates its call for two more 25bp rate hikes by the Federal Reserve--in December 2026 and March 2027--to reach a peak of of 4.25%-4.50% by the first quarter next year. A third hike could come earlier in January, GS says. The Fed may also deliver more than three hikes if the next two inflation reports don't show signs of improvement. Fed officials continued to view inflation risks as skewed to the upside, flagging "the possibility that longer-run inflation expectations could have become unanchored after five years' worth of elevated inflation" as a salient risk. (jiahui.huang@wsj.com; @ivy_jiahuihuang)

data.title: Prospect Markets Nominates VanEck Canada CEO Kevin Gopaul for Election to Board of Directors
data.description:
Vancouver, British Columbia--(Newsfile Corp. - November 19, 2026) - Prospect Prediction Markets Inc. (OTCQB: MKTSF) (FSE: DEP) ("Prospect Markets" or the "Company") is pleased to announce that Mr. Kevin Gopaul has been nominated for election to the Company's board of directors at its upcoming annual general meeting of shareholders (the "Meeting"), scheduled to be held on December 30, 2026.

Mr. Gopaul currently serves as a strategic advisor to the Company. If elected, he will bring nearly 30 years of experience in capital markets and asset management, including senior leadership roles in the Canadian exchange-traded fund industry.

"Kevin built one of Canada's leading ETF businesses from scratch. He knows how to launch new products, earn the trust of institutions and regulators, and hold a company to the highest governance standards. That's exactly the experience we need on our board as we scale following our U.S. launch."

"I'm pleased to be nominated for election to the board of Prospect Markets. Having worked with the team as a strategic advisor, I look forward to contributing my experience to support the Company's next phase of growth," said Kevin Gopaul.

About Mr. Gopaul

Mr. Gopaul has nearly 30 years of experience in the investment management industry, spanning research, trading, portfolio management and executive leadership. He has been Chief Executive Officer of VanEck Canada Inc. since April 2026.

Before that, he spent more than 14 years at BMO Global Asset Management, where he helped build BMO Exchange Traded Funds from its inception into one of Canada's leading ETF businesses, surpassing $100 billion in assets. His roles at BMO included Global Head of Exchange Traded Funds, CEO and Country Head for Canada, and Chief Investment Officer for Canada, overseeing investment teams in Hong Kong, London and Chicago.

Earlier in his career, Mr. Gopaul held senior roles with Barclays Global Investors, Scotia Capital and Sun Life Financial, working across both institutional and retail investor channels.

Mr. Gopaul has been an active contributor to the Canadian financial services industry. He was the founding and longest-serving director of the Canadian ETF Association (CETFA) and has served on the Public Policy Committee of the Canadian Coalition for Good Governance (CCGG).

Mr. Gopaul's appointment as a director is subject to shareholder approval at the Meeting and applicable regulatory requirements.

About Prospect Markets

Prospect Markets is the prediction market platform built natively for sports. From the world's largest leagues to niche competitions, Prospect turns every sports moment into a tradable market. Fans trade peer-to-peer on outcomes using real-time data from our second-screen experience which transforms passive viewership into active market participation.

data.title: Korean Drama Producers Likely to Benefit From China Trade Talks — Market Talk
data.description: Korean drama producers could get a significant earnings boost if Chinese streaming platforms resume buying older shows, DS Investment & Securities analysts say. Studio Dragon and SBS's Studio S, which have excluded China from global streaming-rights sales in recent years, stand to reap substantial gains from licensing their back catalogs there. Recent Seoul-Beijing talks expanded the scope for joint productions to include TV dramas. The next sign of a broader reopening would be advance sales of new dramas to Chinese platforms, helping producers recoup costs before airing, the analysts say. Still, it is "too early to interpret the conclusion of the talks as a full lifting of restrictions on Korean content." Studio Dragon shares jump 30% and SBS adds 8.9%. (jihye.lee@wsj.com)

data.title: Humyn Labs Raises $47 Mn From Accel, Prosus Ventures & Others
data.description:
The funding will support three areas, deployment readiness infrastructure in Brazil, Korea and India, the company’s capture hardware and enrichment engine and on-the-ground presence in San Francisco, London and Seoul

Humyn Labs, a physical AI research and deployment company, today announced USD 47 million in Series A funding. The Company accelerates the deployment readiness of robots in real-world environments across Brazil, South Korea, and India.

The USD 47 million round comprises USD 26 million in equity led by Accel, with participation from Prosus Ventures, BeeGlobal, Finserv Intelligence through Bajaj Finance, Bajaj Alts AI Opportunities Fund, Dallas Venture Capital, Lighthouse Canton, Jump Trading LLC and marquee angel investor Anita Pramoda, former CFO of Epic, who is deeply invested in the Physical AI model stack. The USD 21 million venture debt round was led by Lighthouse Canton with participation from Trifecta Capital.

Humyn Labs has surpassed USD 50 million in annualised revenue within six months of operations. It works with frontier AI labs, robotics companies and world-model developers, and runs its own capture and enrichment operations across 20+ countries in Latin America, East Asia, and South and Southeast Asia.

The funding will support three areas, deployment readiness infrastructure in Brazil, Korea and India; the company’s capture hardware and enrichment engine; and on-the-ground presence in San Francisco, London and Seoul.

Humyn Labs was founded in 2026 by serial entrepreneurs Manish Agarwal, an alumnus of IIM Ahmedabad, and Ishank Gupta, an alumnus of The Wharton School. The company accelerates deployment readiness for Physical AI by turning human experience into physical understanding for robots by capturing real-world work across factories, warehouses, farms and homes.

The company’s proprietary capture devices record how people perform specific jobs to the labs’ requirements, while its end-to-end data engine converts these into labelled, training-ready datasets with verified provenance across sight, sound, motion and touch.

Commenting on this, Manish Agarwal, Co-founder, Humyn Labs, said, “Physical AI will only be as good as the real-world data it learns from. This funding will help us strengthen our research, build trust with labs and enterprises, and expand our global presence. With a USD 10 billion opportunity emerging in data infrastructure, we aim to build a USD 1 billion annual revenue business and establish ourselves as a global leader in the space.”

Ishank Gupta, Co-founder, Humyn Labs, said, “A robot does not learn a job from the internet. It learns it from the person who has done it for twenty years, on the floor where it will be done. We bring the model lab and the site operator onto that floor together, so every deployment teaches the next model, and the world’s factories, farms and warehouses become the training set.”

Speaking on the funding round, Pratik Agarwal, Partner, Accel said, “Physical AI is going to be one of the defining technology shifts of the next decade, and data and deployment are where the real moat will be built. Humyn Labs has the technical depth, the customer pull, and the ambition to be a category leader. We led this round because we believe in the team for the long haul, and we’ll be working closely with them as they expand globally.”

data.title: Adani Green Faces Scrutiny Over Tarali Project As Wildlife Clearance Remains Pending
data.description:
The 1,500-MW Maharashtra project has triggered questions over land classification, project cost disclosures and wildlife-related obligations, even as the company maintains that it does not involve protected or forest land

Adani Green Energy (AGEL) has rejected allegations that its 1,500-MW Tarali pumped storage project in Maharashtra overlaps with protected areas or forest land, as questions over its project cost disclosures and pending wildlife clearance bring regulatory scrutiny to the renewable energy development. The company said the project is located entirely on private, non-forest land, approximately 3.2 km from the Koyna Wildlife Sanctuary in Satara district. It also maintained that the project does not fall within the notified buffer zone of the Sahyadri Tiger Reserve or affect any notified tiger corridor or eco-sensitive zone.

The clarification comes amid controversy over the project's declared cost, which reportedly changed from Rs 5,675 crore to Rs 56.75 crore in a wildlife-related proposal. Adani Green has denied that the difference was intended to reduce its mandatory wildlife conservation contribution.

Cost Dispute Puts Regulatory Compliance In Focus

The controversy centres on the difference between the project's estimated capital cost of Rs 5,675 crore and the Rs 56.75 crore figure mentioned in a wildlife-related filing. Adani Green said the lower amount represented expenditure on preliminary surveys, investigations, geological exploration and feasibility-related activities, rather than a revised estimate of the entire project.

The difference has financial implications for wildlife conservation obligations. According to reports, the proposed contribution could fall from Rs 227 crore to Rs 2.27 crore if calculated against the two respective cost figures. The company has maintained that the State Board for Wildlife considered the project's overall cost at Rs 5,675 crore.

The matter has attracted regulatory attention. The Union Ministry of Environment, Forest and Climate Change directed the Maharashtra Forest Department on 6 November 2026 to investigate the cost discrepancy. The Maharashtra Forest Department subsequently issued a stop-work notice on 13 November, citing the absence of approval from the National Board for Wildlife (NBWL). Following a meeting with Adani Group officials on 17 November, the state Forest Minister directed the company to fulfil all applicable regulatory and financial obligations.

The final decision on the cost discrepancy and associated conservation contribution remains pending. Adani Green said it had received a no-forest-land certificate on 23 January 2024, Environmental Clearance on 11 February 2025 and Consent to Establish from the Maharashtra Pollution Control Board on 7 April 2025. However, the wildlife-clearance proposal remains under consideration by the NBWL.

Storage Demand Raises Project Significance

The developments come at a time when pumped storage is becoming increasingly important to India's renewable energy expansion. These projects store surplus electricity by pumping water to an elevated reservoir and release it through turbines when electricity demand rises or renewable generation falls. According to the Ministry of Power, India had 7.43 GW of operational pumped storage capacity as of August 2026, while another 15.87 GW across 11 projects was under construction or implementation. The country has identified a potential of 345.38 GW across 320 pumped storage projects.

The growing project pipeline reflects the need for long-duration energy storage as solar and wind generation increase. However, the Tarali controversy highlights the importance of transparent project-cost disclosures, environmental assessments and wildlife compliance. For developers, delays in statutory approvals can affect construction schedules, capital deployment and project economics. The outcome of the Tarali case could therefore draw attention from investors and renewable energy companies pursuing large-scale storage infrastructure in ecologically sensitive regions.

data.title: Energean posts 54% jump in nine-month profit helped by higher oil prices
data.description:
Eastern Mediterranean gas producer Energean on Thursday posted a 54% jump in profit in the nine months to September 30 helped by higher oil prices and strong performance from its operated Italian oil fields.

  • The company said realised liquids prices rose 44% to $88 per barrel, driven by stronger oil markets and reported net profit of $317 million in the nine months to September 30 compared with $206 million a year ago

  • Energean stuck to its production forecast for the year

  • The company said Katlan, its offshore gas development in Israel, remains on track for first gas in the second quarter of 2027, with total development spending expected at about $1.25 billion

  • The company declared a third-quarter dividend of 10 cents per share and said it expects to return about $110 million to shareholders in 2026

  • Talks between the London-listed company and BP on the sale of BP's Egyptian oil and gas assets have stalled due to a lack of support from Egyptian authorities, Reuters reported earlier this week
